## Summary

Make `env_vars` passed to `Sandbox.create(...)` visible to later
`commands.run(...)` / `run_code(...)`, by treating them as **sandbox runtime
metadata** and syncing them into the guest through envd's native
`POST :49983/init` at create/restore time.

This is an independent redesign of the previously rejected #484. It is based on
current `master` (single commit, no dependency on #484) and drops the
rootfs/profile/bind-mount injection entirely, following the direction requested
in that review.

## Background

Previously `env_vars` from the SDK were dropped at the CubeAPI layer
(`containers: vec![]`), so they never reached the guest and were invisible to
`commands.run`. #484 tried to fix this by writing
`/etc/profile.d/99-cube-create-env.sh` into the guest rootfs, which was rejected
as too hacky and not a runtime-layer solution.

## Approach

`env_vars` are carried as runtime metadata and injected into envd, the same way
the upstream E2B orchestrator does it (`POST /init` -> envd `defaults.EnvVars`).
envd then merges them when it spawns any process, so the precedence
`create env < per-command env` holds for every process model, not just login
shells.

- **CubeAPI** (`sandboxes.rs`): serialize `env_vars` into the
  `cube.master.sandbox.create_env_vars` annotation (JSON object) instead of
  dropping them.
- **CubeMaster**: the annotation is forwarded to Cubelet via the existing
  `cube.master` prefix passthrough, and stripped in
  `normalizeStoredTemplateRequest` on template commit so per-instance secrets
  are never persisted into template snapshots.
- **Cubelet** (`envd_init.go`): after the readiness probe, `POST /init` to
  `<sandbox-ip>:49983` with the create `env_vars` (bounded retry). envd stores
  them additively (`defaults.EnvVars.Store`), so env already present in the
  guest runtime (e.g. template env) is preserved.

No changes to envd (pinned `e2b-dev/infra@2026.16`); this only wires up the
client side that CubeSandbox was missing compared to the official platform.

## How this addresses the previous review

| Review concern (#484) | This PR |
| --- | --- |
| Solve env sync at the sandbox/runtime layer, not via shell profile | envd `/init` -> `defaults.EnvVars`, merged at the exec layer for every spawned process |
| Don't persist secrets into rootfs/profile files | Nothing written to disk; annotation is in-memory metadata and stripped on template commit |
| Profile `export` overrides per-command `env=` (broken precedence) | envd applies `defaults.EnvVars` first, per-command last -> per-command correctly overrides |
| Shell parsing / injection risk | No shell script generated; env passed as a JSON map |
| Coupling across start/restore/netfile/hostdir/rootfs | One new file + one hook after the probe + annotation passthrough + commit strip |
| Tied to `/bin/bash -l` + `/etc/profile.d`, not general | Independent of shell type / entrypoint; applies to all envd-spawned processes |
| API/Master propagation is a useful part | Kept (CubeAPI -> annotation -> CubeMaster passthrough) |
| Don't merge Cubelet profile/rootfs/bind-mount injection | Removed entirely |

## Precedence

`template env < create env < per-command env`.
Template env already lives in the guest runtime today; `/init` only adds the
create-time keys on top (same-key create overrides template), and envd's
per-command env still overrides both. Docker image `ENV` is not surfaced to
`commands.run`, matching upstream envd behavior (see e2b-dev/infra#2268).

## Tests

Unit tests were added at every layer (all green):

- **Cubelet** `envd_init_test.go`: no-annotation no-op, invalid-JSON error,
  empty-IP error, success path asserting the `envVars`/`timestamp` sent to a
  stub `/init`, and retry-then-succeed.
- **CubeMaster** `store_test.go`: `normalizeStoredTemplateRequest` strips the
  create-env annotation on commit while preserving unrelated annotations.
- **CubeAPI** `sandboxes.rs`: annotation key uses the `cube.master` prefix,
  absent/empty maps are skipped, and a non-empty map serializes to a JSON
  object.

Build/format verified via the project toolchain: `cargo build`/`cargo test`,
`go build`/`go vet`, and `gofmt` + `cargo fmt` clean.

## Notes

- The `/init` body only sends `envVars` + `timestamp`; all other fields are
  omitted, so it never clears envd's access token, default user/workdir, etc.
  (CubeSandbox runs envd without an access token, so first-time `/init` is
  authorized.)
- Covers create and restore-from-snapshot (the normal create-from-template
  path runs the same probe + sync). Across pause/resume of the same VM the env
  persists in guest memory, so no extra resume hook is required.

body:
## Summary

Pausing a sandbox already reclaims its host CPU/RAM (the MicroVM is
snapshotted to disk and shut down), but the node still reserved that quota
against the scheduler, so pausing idle sandboxes did **not** free capacity for
new ones. This PR adds an opt-in, node-local **ratio** that lets operators
control how much of a paused sandbox's CPU/memory quota is released back to the
scheduler, trading resume guarantees for density. Default behaviour is
unchanged.

## Problem

`aggregateAllocated()` sums each sandbox's `HostCpuQ`/`HostMemQ` whenever
`isContainerInGoodState()` is true, and that helper treats `PAUSED`/`PAUSING`
as occupied. The inflated `quota_mem_mb_usage` flows through the cubemaster
heartbeat into the node's `QuotaMemUsage`, so `memFilter` keeps rejecting new
sandboxes even though the capacity is physically free. Net effect: pausing idle
sandboxes gives you nothing back.

## Solution

Add a single node-local knob `host.quota.paused_resource_release_ratio`
(`[0,1]`, default `0`), applied symmetrically to CPU and memory:

| Ratio | Meaning | Resume |
|-------|---------|--------|
| `0.0` (default) | release nothing — paused keeps full quota | guaranteed (legacy behaviour, zero-value safe) |
| `1.0` | release everything — maximum density | best-effort |
| `0 < r < 1` | release `r`, reserve `(1-r)` as headroom | best-effort, only the released fraction is checked |

When the ratio is `> 0`:

- **`aggregateAllocated`**: paused/pausing sandboxes count only `(1-ratio)` of
  their CPU/memory quota and are no longer counted as running, dropping the
  node's reported usage so the scheduler can place new sandboxes into the freed
  capacity. Disk still counts (the pause snapshot occupies storage) and
  `MvmNum` still counts them (the object lives on).
- **`UpdateWithResume`**: resume becomes best-effort. A local, real-time
  admission check rejects the resume when the node can no longer fit the
  released fraction of the sandbox, preventing host memory overcommit / OOM.

Because the reserved `(1-ratio)` portion still shows up in
`QuotaCpuUsage`/`QuotaMemUsage`, a pause-heavy node is naturally deprioritised
by the cpu/mem quota scoring factors, so the scheduler stops piling new
sandboxes onto nodes that already hold many paused ones. A ratio in `(0,1)`
thus gives both density and resume headroom without any cubemaster change.

## Client-facing error

The capacity rejection is returned as `Conflict` (130409) instead of
`TaskResumeFailed`. CubeAPI maps `Conflict` to **HTTP 409** and now forwards the
backend's own reason string verbatim (the 409 branch previously used a
hard-coded message that discarded the detail). Resume rejection is an expected,
retriable state, so 409 is the right class rather than a misleading 500.
Existing SDKs and the WebUI surface a meaningful
`resume rejected ... need X > quota Y` message and can distinguish a capacity
conflict from a backend error — **no client code changes required**.

## Scope / why no cubemaster change

Both the accounting and the resume-admission logic are node-local (resume does
not traverse the scheduler), so cubemaster needs no changes. This targets
high-density, mostly-idle agent fleets (e.g. thousands of digital-employee
agents): idle sandboxes can be paused to free scheduling capacity and resumed
later on a best-effort basis, maximising utilisation.

## Tests

The accounting and admission logic are extracted into pure functions
(`aggregateSandboxResources`, `pausedReserveFactor`, `resumeQuotaRejection`)
with unit tests covering the zero/one/partial ratios, the `PAUSING` transient,
quota boundaries, ratio clamping, and the policy-disabled no-op.

## Config

```yaml
host:
  quota:
    # Fraction of a paused sandbox's CPU/memory quota to release back to the
    # scheduler. 0.0 (default) keeps legacy guaranteed-resume behaviour.
    paused_resource_release_ratio: 0.0

## Summary

When redoing a template image, the artifact-cached `GeneratedRequestJSON` carries the **original source template ID**, not the **redo template ID**. Previously the code reused this stale request, causing template ID mismatches during replica creation and template definition.

## Changes

### `redo.go`
- Pass template ID through `newRedoWorkingRequest` so working requests carry the correct redo template ID
- Always regenerate the sandbox request via `generateTemplateCreateRequest` instead of reusing the artifact-cached `GeneratedRequestJSON`
- Treat undecodable image config as a hard error instead of silently falling back to an empty config
- **Validate** that the generated request template ID matches the redo target template ID before proceeding

### `template_image.go`
- Add `templateID` parameter to `newRedoWorkingRequest` and set it on the working request
- Set `sourceReq.TemplateID` to the normalized template ID in `SubmitRedoTemplateFromImage`

### `template_image_test.go`
- Add `TestRunRedoTemplateImageJobRegeneratesRequestForRedoTemplateID`: verifies that when the artifact carries a stale template ID, the redo still generates a request with the correct redo template ID

### `cube-egress-start.sh`
- Pin CubeEgress default image tag from `latest` to `v0.4.0` for deterministic deployments

## Test Plan
- New unit test covers the stale-template-ID scenario end-to-end through the redo job flow
- Verified generated request carries correct template ID, artifact URL, and image config commands

body:
## Problem
In a multi-replica cubemaster deployment, node metadata (labels, capacity, instance type, component versions, etc.) registered on one replica was never visible to other replicas.

The root cause: `loopReload` — the goroutine responsible for periodically syncing node metadata from MySQL into the in-memory map — was never started in `Init()`. Each replica only knew about nodes that contacted it directly, so scheduling decisions on other replicas operated on an incomplete view of the cluster.

A secondary bug compounded the problem: even if the goroutine had been running, `reload()` replaced the entire in-memory map with a DB snapshot (`s.nodes = next`). This meant any heartbeat that arrived on the current replica during the DB scan would be silently overwritten, potentially causing a healthy node to briefly appear unhealthy.

### Bug - loopReload goroutine never started
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Node["Cubelet Node"]

    subgraph ReplicaA["CubeMaster Replica A"]
        RA_Reg["RegisterNode /\nUpdateNodeStatus"]
        RA_Mem["in-memory global.nodes\n✅ updated"]
        RA_MySQL_Write["MySQL write\n✅ persisted"]
    end

    subgraph ReplicaB["CubeMaster Replica B"]
        RB_Loop["❌ loopReload\nNEVER STARTED in Init()"]
        RB_Mem["in-memory global.nodes\n❌ stays empty forever"]
        RB_Sched["Scheduler\n❌ incomplete cluster view"]
    end

    MySQL[("MySQL")]

    Node -->|"register / heartbeat"| RA_Reg
    RA_Reg --> RA_MySQL_Write
    RA_Reg --> RA_Mem
    RA_MySQL_Write --> MySQL

    MySQL -.->|"sync never triggered"| RB_Loop
    RB_Loop -.->|"goroutine not running"| RB_Mem
    RB_Mem --> RB_Sched

    style RB_Loop fill:#ffcccc,color:#000
    style RB_Mem fill:#ffcccc,color:#000
    style RB_Sched fill:#ffcccc,color:#000
    style ReplicaA fill:#dceefb,color:#000
    style ReplicaB fill:#fff0f0,color:#000
    style MySQL fill:#f5a623,color:#000
```
**Consequence:** Replica B never learns about nodes registered on Replica A. Its scheduler operates on an empty or stale node list, causing missed scheduling opportunities or incorrect "no available node" errors.

## Fix
**Start the sync goroutine**
A dd `go global.loopReload(ctx)` in `Init()`. The goroutine fires every`SyncMetaDataInterval` (default 30 s) and pulls the latest state fromMySQL into `global.nodes`.

 **Replace full map swap with a field-level merge**
Introduce `applyReloadResult()` with the following strategy:
- *Registration fields* (labels, capacity, instance type, quota, versions, etc.) always take the DB value. `RegisterNode` and `persistVersions` write to MySQL before updating in-memory state, so the DB is the authoritative source for these fields.
- *Heartbeat / status fields* (`HeartbeatTime`, `Conditions`, `ReportedReady`) keep the in-memory value when it is fresher than the DB snapshot. This prevents a slow DB scan from overwriting a heartbeat that arrived on this replica while the scan was in progress.
- *New nodes* (present in DB but absent in the in-memory map) are added directly — this is the primary cross-replica sync path.

### Fix — Replace full map swap with field-level merge

#### When does the problem occur?

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Node as Cubelet Node
    participant DB as MySQL
    participant Mem as Replica Memory

    Note over DB,Mem: reload() begins — scans DB, captures snapshot at T0

    DB->>Mem: next["node-a"].HeartbeatTime = T0  (snapshot)

    Node->>DB: heartbeat T1 arrives (T1 > T0), written to DB
    Node->>Mem: HeartbeatTime = T1 written to memory

    Note over Mem: Memory is now ahead of snapshot: T1 > T0 ✅

    Note over Mem: reload() finishes — applies s.nodes = next ❌
    Mem->>Mem: HeartbeatTime overwritten: T1 → T0 💥

    Note over Mem: applyCurrentHealth sees stale T0
    Note over Mem: now - T0 > healthTimeout → Healthy = false ❌
    Note over Mem: node excluded from scheduling 🚫
```

The race window opens whenever a heartbeat is written to DB and memory **after** the reload scan has already read past that row, but **before** `s.nodes = next` is applied. With a 30 s reload interval and hundreds of nodes heartbeating every 10 s, this window is hit on virtually every reload cycle.

#### How the fix works
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start(["applyReloadResult(next)"])
    Loop["for each nodeID in next"]
    Exists{"nodeID exists\nin s.nodes?"}

    subgraph ExistingPath["Existing node — field-level merge"]
        RegFields["Registration fields\nlabels / capacity / instanceType\nquota / hostIP / grpcPort / versions\n──────────────────────────\nAlways take DB value\nDB write happens before memory write\nso DB is always ≥ memory"]
        HBCheck{"newSnap.HeartbeatTime\n> existing.HeartbeatTime?"}
        TakeDB["Take DB heartbeat fields\nConditions / Images\nLocalTemplates / ReportedReady"]
        KeepMem["Keep in-memory heartbeat fields\nin-memory is fresher —\nheartbeat arrived during DB scan"]
        Health["applyCurrentHealth(existing)"]
    end

    subgraph NewPath["New node — cross-replica discovery"]
        AddNode["s.nodes[nodeID] = newSnap\nnode registered on another replica"]
    end

    Start --> Loop --> Exists
    Exists -->|yes| RegFields
    RegFields --> HBCheck
    HBCheck -->|yes| TakeDB --> Health
    HBCheck -->|no| KeepMem --> Health
    Exists -->|no| AddNode

    style ExistingPath fill:#e8f4e8,color:#000
    style NewPath fill:#dceefb,color:#000
    style HBCheck fill:#fff9e6,color:#000
    style KeepMem fill:#d4edda,color:#000
    style TakeDB fill:#d4edda,color:#000
    style AddNode fill:#cce5ff,color:#000
```

## How node data is synchronized across cubemaster replicas when fixed
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Node["Cubelet Node"]

    subgraph ReplicaA["CubeMaster Replica A (receives request)"]
        RA_Reg["RegisterNode /\nUpdateNodeStatus"]
        RA_Mem["in-memory\nglobal.nodes"]
        RA_LC["localcache"]
        RA_Metric["fanOutResourceMetric"]
    end

    subgraph Storage["Shared Storage"]
        MySQL[("MySQL\nnode_registrations\nnode_status\nnode_component_versions")]
        Redis[("Redis\nNodeMetric")]
    end

    subgraph ReplicaB["CubeMaster Replica B (sync)"]
        RB_Loop["loopReload\nevery SyncMetaDataInterval"]
        RB_Merge["applyReloadResult()\n───────────────────────────\nregistration fields → DB wins\nversions          → DB wins\nheartbeat fields  → fresher wins\nnew node          → add directly"]
        RB_Mem["in-memory\nglobal.nodes"]
        RB_LC["localcache\nloop / loopUpdateMetric"]
    end

    Node -->|"register / heartbeat"| RA_Reg
    RA_Reg -->|"1 write first"| MySQL
    RA_Reg -->|"2 update"| RA_Mem
    RA_Mem -->|"syncLocalcache"| RA_LC

    RA_Reg -->|"resource metrics only"| RA_Metric
    RA_Metric -->|"WriteNodeMetric"| Redis
    RA_Metric -->|"UpdateNodeMetricInProcess"| RA_LC

    MySQL -->|"every SyncMetaDataInterval"| RB_Loop
    RB_Loop --> RB_Merge
    RB_Merge -->|"merge"| RB_Mem

    Redis -->|"loopUpdateMetric tick"| RB_LC
    RB_Mem -->|"ListSchedulerNodes\nevery SyncMetaDataInterval"| RB_LC

    style MySQL fill:#f5a623,color:#000
    style Redis fill:#d0021b,color:#fff
    style RB_Merge fill:#e8f4e8,color:#000
    style ReplicaA fill:#dceefb,color:#000
    style ReplicaB fill:#fdf3e3,color:#000
    style Storage fill:#f9f9f9,color:#000
```

| Data type | Cross-replica sync path | Latency |
|-----------|------------------------|---------|
| Registration / Versions | MySQL → loopReload → applyReloadResult | ≤ SyncMetaDataInterval |
| Heartbeat / Status | MySQL → loopReload → applyReloadResult (fresher wins) | ≤ SyncMetaDataInterval |
| Resource Metrics | Redis → loopUpdateMetric | near real-time (50 ms tick) |


## Testing
Five new unit tests added in `service_reload_test.go`, all exercising `applyReloadResult()` directly (no DB required):
- `TestApplyReloadResultUpdatesRegistrationFields` — labels, instance type, IP, port and quota fields are updated from the DB snapshot
- `TestApplyReloadResultPreservesInMemoryHeartbeatWhenFresher` — a fresher in-memory heartbeat is not overwritten by a stale DB value
- `TestApplyReloadResultTakesDBHeartbeatWhenFresher` — a fresher DB heartbeat is correctly applied to the in-memory snapshot
- `TestApplyReloadResultSyncsVersionsForExistingNode` — component versions and their content hash are synced from DB for existing nodes
- `TestApplyReloadResultAddsNewNodeFromDB` — a node registered on another replica is discovered and added to the local in-memory map

- `CubeEgress/lua/admin.lua`: extend `/admin/v1/health` with `version`/`commit`/`build_time` fields

### Layer 2: Release manifest & deploy
- `deploy/one-click/build-release-bundle.sh`: add `cube-egress` to `release-manifest.json` components; write host-side `cube-egress/version` marker file
- `deploy/one-click/install.sh`: copy `cube-egress/` directory on compute-role nodes

- `Cubelet/pkg/cubelet/versioninfo/collector_test.go`: 2 new tests (marker present → reported; marker absent → silent skip)

## Design
- Version follows `cube_version` (same as all other components), ensuring `versionIsDeclared()` consistency in CubeMaster
- Graceful degradation: missing version marker file → component silently omitted (never blocks heartbeat)

cleanupHostDirVolumes walked sandboxDir using the logical path joined from hostDirBasePath. When any ancestor of hostDirBasePath is a symlink (e.g. /data -> /mnt/ssd/data), the kernel records the fully resolved mountpoint in /proc/self/mountinfo, so IsMountPoint's string comparison never matched. body:
Add `cubecli cubebox logs <sandbox-id>` to read container stdout/stderr from inside the cubelet mount namespace.

Features:
- Default: last 100 lines of stdout
- --all / -a: print full log
- --tail N: last N lines
- --head N: first N lines
- --stderr / -e: read stderr instead of stdout

Implementation:
The log files live at:
  /data/cubelet/state/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/default/<id>/stdout|stderr

They are inside the cubelet mount namespace, so the process must call setns(2) to enter it.  Go's scheduler can move goroutines between OS threads, making a plain setns from Go unsafe.  Instead, the logs command re-execs itself with CUBEMNT=1 and CUBECLI_LOGS_MODE=1; the existing C constructor in pkg/cubemnt/nsenter.c enters the mount namespace before any Go code runs, ensuring all threads are in the correct namespace. Other subcommands are unaffected.

…cation in scheduling

Sandbox scheduling previously sized each node's schedulable CPU/Mem from the node-reported quota minus the per-node allocated usage recorded in Redis, with no way to overcommit or to opt out of the Redis allocation records. This made it hard to densify placement without editing node-side factors.

Add two scheduler config knobs and wire them through the filter and score plugins so capacity is computed consistently:

- ignore_redis_allocation (default false): treat the Redis-recorded allocated CPU/Mem as 0 during scheduling.
- overcommit_ratio (default CPU=3, Mem=2) with optional per-instance-type overrides via overcommit_ratio_conf, applied to the node-reported quota.

Helper methods default unset values, sanitize non-positive ratios back to the defaults, and keep filter and score plugins aligned. Physical load guards (CPU util ceiling, real-time free memory) are intentionally left untouched to avoid scheduling onto truly overloaded nodes.

Implement a log forwarding mechanism that streams container init process stdout/stderr from the agent to the host shim, persisting output to /run/vc/vm/<sandbox_id>/stdout and /run/vc/vm/<sandbox_id>/stderr.

Key design points:
- shim injects cube.container.log_forwarding=true annotation into the OCI spec so the agent creates stdout/stderr pipes instead of leaving them pointed at /dev/null
- shim opens a dedicated vsock connection for log streaming so the control-plane RPC connection is never blocked
- log forwarding is started after container start (cold boot) and restarted automatically after resume; it is cleanly cancelled before pause/snapshot via a watch channel so the vsock read loop exits before the VM is frozen
- during template (app-snapshot) creation the annotation is still injected so the agent creates the pipes, but the shim does not start forwarding; pipes buffer output until the first restore
- stdout/stderr files are opened with create+append so they survive across pause/resume cycles; parent directory is created if absent
- exec_id passed to read_stdout/read_stderr is empty string to address the init process (non-empty id would look up a named exec process)

body:
## Motivation

While troubleshooting a local network issue, I found that the effective sandbox CIDR can still conflict with the host network even when `ip route` does not make the conflict obvious.

In particular, the default Cubelet sandbox CIDR can overlap with host DNS resolver addresses such as `192.168.0.1`. When that happens, host DNS traffic may be routed through the sandbox network instead of the real LAN path, breaking host-side DNS resolution and causing operations such as image pulls to fail.

CubeSandbox `v0.3.1` already added preflight validation for `CUBE_SANDBOX_NETWORK_CIDR` when users explicitly override the CIDR. This leaves the default-CIDR path uncovered, because the installer previously skipped conflict validation when `CUBE_SANDBOX_NETWORK_CIDR` was not set.

This PR extends that protection to the remaining gap:

- validate the effective sandbox CIDR even when the user does not set `CUBE_SANDBOX_NETWORK_CIDR`
- detect conflicts not only from host interfaces and routes, but also from host resolver nameservers

## What Changed

- extract the packaged one-click bundle earlier so `install.sh` can read the packaged Cubelet `config.toml` and fail during preflight before stopping or replacing the existing deployment
- when `CUBE_SANDBOX_NETWORK_CIDR` is unset, read the default CIDR from the packaged Cubelet network plugin config and run the same preflight validation instead of skipping it
- extend CIDR conflict detection to check common host resolver sources:
  - `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf`
  - `/run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf`
  - `/run/NetworkManager/no-stub-resolv.conf`
  - `/var/run/NetworkManager/no-stub-resolv.conf`
  - `/run/resolvconf/resolv.conf`
  - `/etc/resolvconf/run/resolv.conf`
  - `/etc/resolv.conf`
- avoid reporting known Cube-owned leftover devices such as `cube-dev` and `z<ip>` as host LAN conflicts during reinstall / recovery paths

## Design Note

This PR currently excludes known Cube-owned leftover virtual devices such as `cube-dev` and `z<ip>` from the host conflict check.

This is intended to keep reinstall / recovery paths usable when stale Cube-owned devices are present, while still detecting conflicts with the real host LAN, routes, and resolver nameservers.

If you prefer to keep explicit manual cleanup for old Cube virtual devices, I can drop this part and keep the PR focused only on:

- validating the packaged default CIDR when no override is set
- checking resolver nameservers in addition to interfaces / routes
- running that validation before the installer stops the existing deployment

## Validation

Real machine validation:

- confirmed that `install.sh` now fails before stopping the existing deployment when the packaged default CIDR `192.168.0.0/18` overlaps with host resolver nameservers such as `192.168.0.1`
- confirmed that the installer continues past preflight when the effective sandbox CIDR does not overlap with host interfaces, routes, or resolver nameservers
- confirmed that resolver overlap is now rejected during preflight instead of surfacing later as host-side DNS failures, such as image pull failures on the host machine
- confirmed the conflict is reported from the real resolver files, for example:
  - `/run/NetworkManager/no-stub-resolv.conf`
  - `/var/run/NetworkManager/no-stub-resolv.conf`
  - `/etc/resolv.conf`

Focused shell test:

```bash
bash deploy/one-click/tests/test_cidr_preflight.sh
```

This test covers:

- host interface overlap
- host route overlap
- resolver nameserver overlap
- avoiding false positives from known Cube-owned leftover devices
- reading the default CIDR from packaged Cubelet config
- ensuring preflight runs before the script stops the existing deployment

## Scope

This PR is limited to one-click CIDR preflight behavior. It does not change the CIDR format validation, mask validation, or alignment checks.

The existing `CUBE_SANDBOX_NETWORK_CIDR_SKIP_CONFLICT_CHECK` bypass remains unchanged.

body:
## Summary

Template compatibility governance: addresses the core pain point of "templates silently break after an upgrade with no warning." Guest-image and cube-agent versions are bound at template creation time, compatibility is automatically scanned and stale replicas are flagged after upgrades, a node×template compatibility matrix is exposed, and stale templates are hard-blocked before sandbox creation with actionable error messages.

> **Note**: One-click batch rebuild is out of scope for this PR and will follow separately.

---

## Design Decisions

| # | Decision | Rationale |
|---|----------|-----------|
| D1 | Version binding at the replica level, new columns on `t_cube_template_replica`, **fingerprint unchanged** | A replica is the physical snapshot unit for node × template; fingerprint remains scoped to ext4 rootfs reuse |
| D2 | kernel version **excluded** from compatibility evaluation | Guest kernel files are copied into the template directory at creation time; changing the kernel does not affect existing template usability |
| D3 | Compatibility dimensions: **guest-image + cube-agent** | cube-agent is compiled into `/sbin/init` at build time; together with guest-image they determine whether a sandbox can start |
| D4 | Compatibility state machine: `OK` / `STALE` / `UNKNOWN`, conservative by default | Historical replicas without bound versions → `UNKNOWN` (not blocked); only confirmed mismatches → `STALE` |
| D5 | Scanning driven by version-report changes + periodic reconciler as fallback | Does not depend on the upgrade orchestrator; any path that changes the guest version is detected |
| D6 | Bound versions sourced exclusively from cubelet RPC responses | The snapshot captures the guest actually running on the node at that moment — most accurate, no heartbeat delay, no race |
| D7 | Single `isReplicaSchedulable` gate across all replica selection paths | Prevents bypasses through `ResolveTemplateReadyReplica`, warm-up, scheduler scoring, or cache registration |
| D8 | Callback-based registration breaks the nodemeta ↔ templatecenter import cycle | Avoids a Go compilation failure from circular imports |

---

## Changes

### Data Model

- **DB Migration `0005`**: 6 new columns on `t_cube_template_replica`:
  - `guest_image_version` VARCHAR(128)
  - `agent_version` VARCHAR(128)
  - `kernel_version` VARCHAR(256) (retained for bookkeeping, excluded from evaluation)
  - `compat_status` VARCHAR(32) DEFAULT 'UNKNOWN'
  - `compat_policy` VARCHAR(32) DEFAULT 'STRICT' (reserved for future agent decoupling)
  - `compat_checked_unix` BIGINT
  - New index `idx_node_compat(node_id, compat_status)`
- GORM model / `ReplicaStatus` / mapping functions extended accordingly
- Compat columns **excluded** from the `replicaStatusUpdateFields` Upsert whitelist; updates go through a dedicated `updateReplicaCompat`

### Version Binding at Template Creation

- **Proto extension**: `AppSnapshotResponse` + `CommitSandboxResponse` gain `guest_image_version` / `agent_version` / `kernel_version` fields
- **Cubelet**: `version_binding.go` — reads current versions from `versioninfo.Collector` during snapshot/commit and returns them in the RPC response
- **CubeMaster**: `bindGuestVersionToReplica` populates bound versions when a replica reaches READY
  - Covers all 3 paths: `createReplicaOnNode` (including redo) / `runTemplateCommitJob` / `runSnapshotCreateJob`
  - Evaluated immediately via `evaluateCompat`; all dimensions present → OK, any missing → UNKNOWN (never falls back to OK)
- **Existing replica backfill**:
  - `adopt-baseline`: operator-initiated → writes current node versions as the baseline for UNKNOWN replicas → OK
  - Batch rebuild entry point (reuses existing redo pipeline)

### Post-Upgrade Compatibility Scanning

- **Event-driven**: `nodemeta.OnGuestAgentVersionChanged` registered callback — triggers a scan immediately when guest-image or cube-agent version changes
- **Periodic fallback**: `startCompatReconciler` scans all READY replicas every 5 minutes (including STALE, so false positives self-heal)
- **Core functions**:
  - `evaluateCompat` — multi-dimension comparison (guest-image + agent, **kernel excluded**), with `normalizeVer` canonicalization
  - `ScanNodeCompat` — re-evaluates all replicas for a single node
  - `updateReplicaCompat` — dedicated column update (guarded by `status='READY'` to avoid races with in-flight creation)
- **Untrusted node handling**: offline / stale heartbeat → `UNKNOWN` (never reuses stale versions, never falsely marks STALE)
- **Cache eviction**: when a replica is marked STALE, `localcache` + `localityCache` entries are evicted synchronously

### Compatibility Matrix API

- **CubeMaster**: `GET /cube/template/compat` — aggregated template × node matrix with `summary` + `templates[].nodes[]`
- **CubeMaster**: `POST /cube/template/compat` — `rescan` / `adopt_baseline` actions
- **CubeAPI**: `GET /cubeapi/v1/templates/compat` — proxy + DTO transformation
- **CubeAPI**: `POST /cubeapi/v1/templates/compat/:templateID/adopt-baseline` — proxy + DTO transformation
- **OpenAPI**: new schemas + paths

### Hard Block Before Sandbox Creation

- **Unified gate**: `isReplicaSchedulable` = `Status==READY && CompatStatus != STALE`
  Wired into all replica selection paths: `EnsureTemplateLocalityReady` / `ResolveTemplateReadyReplica` / `warmReadyTemplateLocality` / scheduler scoring / cache registration / `EnsureReadyReplica`
- **End-to-end error chain** (Go → Rust → SDK → frontend):
  - CubeMaster `sandbox_create.go` → detects `ErrTemplateStaleNeedsRedo` → `ErrorCode_Conflict(130409)`
  - CubeAPI `sandboxes.rs` → maps 130409 → 409 response
  - SDK → identifies by error code
  - WebUI `SandboxNew.tsx` → structured display + CTA to rebuild
- **Conservative**: `UNKNOWN` never blocked (avoids breaking existing replicas); `OK` incurs zero overhead

### WebUI Compatibility Panel

- **Global Banner**: sticky alert below `TopBar` when STALE replicas exist; dismiss stored as a snapshot in `sessionStorage`, auto-reappears when STALE counts change
- **Template Compatibility Tab**: KPI bar + template × node matrix (icon + label + color triple encoding, a11y-friendly)
- **SandboxNew pre-check**: all replicas STALE → card disabled + "go rebuild" CTA; partial STALE → warning only
- **List / detail hints**: card badge, ReplicaTable compat column, STALE row highlight + version diff
- **i18n**: all four compat states, banner, and error messages → `zh` / `en`
- **Overview** gains a stale-template KPI card; `CommandPalette` gains a template-compatibility action

body:
## Motivation

`CubeMaster/pkg/templatecenter/template_image.go` had grown into a ~2,900-line monolithic file mixing image export (`skopeo`/`umoci`), ext4 filesystem creation, rootfs artifact lifecycle, job persistence, template request generation, redo logic, and distribution orchestration. This made the code hard to reason about, test, and extend.

**Goals:**
- Decompose the monolith into focused, testable units with clear boundaries
- Extract a reusable `image/` sub-package for OCI image → ext4 conversion
- Separate job persistence, artifact lifecycle, and distribution into dedicated files
- Preserve all existing behavior and pass existing tests

## Changes

### New sub-package: `image/` — OCI image → ext4 rootfs pipeline

| File | Responsibility |
|------|---------------|
| `image/types.go` | `SourceSpec`, `BuildOptions`, `BuildResult`, `PreparedSource`, Docker/skopeo inspect structs |
| `image/source.go` | `PrepareSource` / `PrepareLocalSource` — image pull via skopeo (daemonless) or docker |
| `image/command.go` | `dockerLogin`, `dockerRun`, `skopeoOutput` — CLI wrappers |
| `image/export.go` | `exportImageRootfs` — unpack OCI image to rootfs via umoci (daemonless) or `docker export` |
| `image/ext4.go` | `BuildExt4` — create ext4 filesystem from rootfs directory tree |
| `image/disk.go` | Streaming ext4 creation, image size estimation, layer inspection |
| `image/paths.go` | Artifact work/store directory layout, disk space safety margins |
| `image/ref.go` | Image reference parsing (`splitImageRef`, `registryHostFromImageRef`), base URL normalization |
| `image/util.go` | `computeFileSHA256`, disk space checks, loop-mount capability detection |
| `image/image_test.go` | ~1,000 lines of tests covering the full pipeline |

### New files in `templatecenter/` — decomposed from `template_image.go`

| File | Responsibility |
|------|---------------|
| `artifact_build.go` | `ensureRootfsArtifact` — idempotent artifact creation with fingerprint-based deduplication and soft-delete restoration |
| `artifact_cleanup.go` | `cleanupFailedRootfsArtifact` — cleanup failed/abandoned artifact records and local files |
| `distribution.go` | `distributeRootfsArtifact`, `cleanupArtifactOnNodes` — distribute artifacts to Cubelet nodes and tear them down |
| `fingerprint.go` | `buildTemplateSpecFingerprint`, `marshalTemplateImageJobRequest` — content-addressable deduplication of template specs and job requests |
| `image_job_runner.go` | `runTemplateImageJob` — the main job state machine orchestrating pull → build → distribute |
| `job_constants.go` | Job phase constants (`PULLING`, `BUILDING`, `DISTRIBUTING`, `READY`, etc.) and sentinel errors |
| `job_dto.go` | `jobModelToInfo`, `artifactModelToInfo` — DB model → API response DTO conversion |
| `job_repo.go` | `getTemplateImageJobRecordByID`, `getRootfsArtifactByFingerprint`, etc. — job and artifact persistence queries |
| `redo.go` | `runRedoTemplateImageJob` — redo orchestration with mode detection (ALL/FAILED/SCOPE), resume-from-phase optimization, scope resolution |
| `request_validation.go` | `normalizeTemplateImageRequest`, `resolveTemplateNodes` — request normalization, node resolution, port validation |
| `template_request.go` | `generateTemplateCreateRequest` — build `CreateCubeSandboxReq` from image config + user overrides |

### Shrunk files

| File | Before | After | Delta |
|------|--------|-------|-------|
| `template_image.go` | ~2,894 lines | 266 lines | **-91%** |
| `template_image_test.go` | ~2,050 lines | 1,138 lines | **-44%** |

`template_image.go` now contains only the top-level public API entry points:
- `SubmitTemplateFromImage` / `SubmitRedoTemplateFromImage`
- `GetTemplateImageJobInfo` / `GetRootfsArtifactInfo` / `OpenRootfsArtifact`

## Architecture

```
templatecenter/
├── image/                    # OCI image → ext4 pipeline (new sub-package)
│   ├── types.go              #   SourceSpec, PreparedSource, BuildResult
│   ├── source.go             #   PrepareSource (skopeo/docker pull)
│   ├── export.go             #   exportImageRootfs (umoci/docker export)
│   ├── ext4.go               #   BuildExt4
│   ├── disk.go               #   streaming ext4, size estimation
│   ├── command.go            #   CLI wrappers (docker, skopeo)
│   ├── paths.go              #   directory layout
│   ├── ref.go                #   image reference parsing
│   └── util.go               #   sha256, disk checks
│
├── template_image.go         # Public API: Submit, GetInfo, OpenArtifact (266 lines)
├── template_request.go       # Request generation from image config
├── request_validation.go     # Normalization & validation
├── artifact_build.go         # Idempotent artifact creation + dedup
├── artifact_cleanup.go       # Failed artifact cleanup
├── distribution.go           # Node-level artifact distribution
├── image_job_runner.go       # Job state machine (pull→build→distribute)
├── job_constants.go          # Phase constants
├── job_dto.go                # DB → API DTO conversion
├── job_repo.go               # Persistence queries
├── redo.go                   # Redo orchestration
└── fingerprint.go            # Content fingerprinting & serialization
```

## Testing

- All existing tests pass (`image/image_test.go`, `template_image_test.go`)
- Tested end-to-end on staging: create template → redo → create sandbox instance → delete template
- No behavioral changes — pure structural refactor

## Checklist

- [x] Build passes (`make cubemaster`)
- [x] All tests pass
- [x] Copyright headers updated to 2026
- [x] No sensitive data (IPs, passwords, local paths) in diff

body:
## What

`CubeAPI`'s `create_sandbox` already promotes the `host-mount` metadata key to a CubeMaster annotation, but everything else in `metadata` falls through to `labels`. Annotations are the only sandbox metadata that reach the shim (and thus influence the guest), so a caller currently has **no way to inject guest kernel cmdline parameters** through the sandbox API.

This promotes the well-known `cube.vm.kernel.cmdline.append` key the same way `host-mount` is promoted.

## Why

`Cubelet` already consumes `cube.vm.kernel.cmdline.append` (`AnnotationVMKernelCmdlineAppend` in `pkg/constants/const.go`) and appends it to the guest boot args — where any guest process can read it from `/proc/cmdline`. The only missing link was the API surface: `create_sandbox` hard-codes `annotations: None` and drops `metadata` into `labels`.

With this change a caller can pass, e.g., a per-sandbox identity/bootstrap datum into the guest **without a shared host mount** — useful for agent runtimes that want the guest to self-identify at boot without an injected file or volume.

## Change

`CubeAPI/src/services/sandboxes.rs`: add the `KERNEL_CMDLINE_APPEND_KEY` const and promote it from `metadata` → `annotations`, mirroring the existing `HOSTDIR_MOUNT_KEY` promotion (the only other promoted key). ~7 lines; no behavior change for existing callers (they don't set this key). `cargo check` passes.

body:
## Summary

Add `com.nodeaffinity.selector` annotation to allow specifying arbitrary `NodeSelectorRequirement` objects when creating a sandbox, enabling custom node affinity rules beyond the predefined cluster label and instance type selectors.

Also add `NodeLabels` field to `node.Node` and merge it into the `Labels()` method, so that labels reported during node registration are visible to the scheduler for affinity matching.

## Changes

### Custom node affinity selector annotation

A new annotation `com.nodeaffinity.selector` accepts a JSON array of `NodeSelectorRequirement` objects. Each object has:

- `key` (string) — the node label key
- `operator` (string) — one of `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, `DoesNotExist`, `Gt`, `Lt`
- `values` (array of strings, optional) — required for `In` and `NotIn`, must be omitted for `Exists` and `DoesNotExist`

The parsed requirements are appended to the `matchExpressions` in `constructNodeAffinity`, alongside existing cluster label and instance type selectors. If the annotation value is invalid JSON, the error is logged and the request proceeds without the custom selector (graceful degradation).

The `NodeSelectorRequirement` struct is unchanged — `Values` remains `map[string]any`. The conversion from JSON array to map happens at the parsing boundary via `valuesSliceToMap`.

### Node labels propagation

Previously, `node.Node.Labels()` only returned 6 hardcoded affinity keys derived from struct fields (`Zone`, `ClusterLabel`, `CPUType`, `MemorySize`, `CPUCores`, `InstanceType`). Custom labels reported by cubelet during node registration were stored in `NodeSnapshot.Labels` and persisted to MySQL, but dropped during the `toSchedulerNode` conversion — making them invisible to the scheduler.

This PR adds a `NodeLabels` field to `node.Node` and propagates `snap.Labels` through `toSchedulerNode` and the localcache update path (`updateNodeFromMetaData`). The `Labels()` method now merges `NodeLabels` on top of the hardcoded keys, so custom labels (e.g. `kubernetes.io/hostname`) become available for affinity matching.

## Examples

### Pin sandbox to a specific host

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:8089/cube/sandbox" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "RequestID": "pin-host-001",
    "instance_type": "cubebox",
    "timeout": 60,
    "containers": [],
    "annotations": {
      "com.nodeaffinity.selector": "[{\"key\":\"kubernetes.io/hostname\",\"operator\":\"In\",\"values\":[\"10.0.0.1\"]}]"
    },
    "network_type": "tap",
    "cubevs_context": {
      "allowInternetAccess": true
    }
  }'
```

### Require a specific instance type (Exists operator)

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:8089/cube/sandbox" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "RequestID": "instance-type-exists-001",
    "instance_type": "cubebox",
    "timeout": 60,
    "containers": [],
    "annotations": {
      "com.nodeaffinity.selector": "[{\"key\":\"kubernetes.io/instance-type\",\"operator\":\"Exists\"}]"
    },
    "network_type": "tap",
    "cubevs_context": {
      "allowInternetAccess": true
    }
  }'
```

### Exclude a zone (NotIn operator)

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:8089/cube/sandbox" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "RequestID": "exclude-zone-001",
    "instance_type": "cubebox",
    "timeout": 60,
    "containers": [],
    "annotations": {
      "com.nodeaffinity.selector": "[{\"key\":\"topology.kubernetes.io/zone\",\"operator\":\"NotIn\",\"values\":[\"zone-a\",\"zone-b\"]}]"
    },
    "network_type": "tap",
    "cubevs_context": {
      "allowInternetAccess": true
    }
  }'
```

### Avoid nodes with a specific label (DoesNotExist operator)

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:8089/cube/sandbox" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "RequestID": "label-does-not-exist-001",
    "instance_type": "cubebox",
    "timeout": 60,
    "containers": [],
    "annotations": {
      "com.nodeaffinity.selector": "[{\"key\":\"kubernetes.io/cpu-type\",\"operator\":\"DoesNotExist\"}]"
    },
    "network_type": "tap",
    "cubevs_context": {
      "allowInternetAccess": true
    }
  }'
```

### Combine with existing annotations

The new selector composes with the existing `com.nodeaffinity.cluster.label` and `com.nodeaffinity.instancetype` annotations. All conditions are ANDed within the same `NodeSelectorTerm`:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:8089/cube/sandbox" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "RequestID": "combined-001",
    "instance_type": "cubebox",
    "timeout": 60,
    "containers": [],
    "annotations": {
      "com.nodeaffinity.cluster.label": "cluster-1",
      "com.nodeaffinity.selector": "[{\"key\":\"kubernetes.io/hostname\",\"operator\":\"In\",\"values\":[\"10.0.0.1\"]},{\"key\":\"kubernetes.io/instance-type\",\"operator\":\"Exists\"}]"
    },
    "network_type": "tap",
    "cubevs_context": {
      "allowInternetAccess": true
    }
  }'
```

### Multiple requirements in one selector

All requirements in the array are ANDed — the node must satisfy every condition:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:8089/cube/sandbox" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "RequestID": "multi-req-001",
    "instance_type": "cubebox",
    "timeout": 60,
    "containers": [],
    "annotations": {
      "com.nodeaffinity.selector": "[{\"key\":\"kubernetes.io/cpu-type\",\"operator\":\"NotIn\",\"values\":[\"intel\"]},{\"key\":\"kubernetes.io/instance-type\",\"operator\":\"Exists\"}]"
    },
    "network_type": "tap",
    "cubevs_context": {
      "allowInternetAccess": true
    }
  }'
```

### Full example with app snapshot annotations

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:8089/cube/sandbox" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "RequestID": "combine-example-001",
    "instance_type": "cubebox",
    "timeout": 60,
    "containers": [],

## Summary

This PR addresses #498 by updating `IPOverrideTransport.handle_request()` to read and buffer the incoming request body before copying it into the proxied request.

This prevents multipart uploads created with `files=` from failing with `httpx.RequestNotRead` before the transport reaches the expected connection attempt.

## Motivation

`IPOverrideTransport.handle_request()` currently copies `request.content` directly when creating the proxied request.

This works for buffered request bodies, but multipart uploads created with `files=` are streaming requests in `httpx`. Accessing `request.content` before the body has been read raises `httpx.RequestNotRead`.

## Changes

- call `request.read()` before copying the request body in `IPOverrideTransport.handle_request()`
- add focused coverage for:
  - `content=bytes`
  - `files=` multipart uploads
  - `GET` requests with no body
- keep the expected final failure mode as `httpx.ConnectError` for the test transport target, ensuring the request-copying path succeeds first

## Validation

Focused test:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=sdk/python \
python -m pytest sdk/python/tests/test_sandbox.py::TestIPOverrideTransport -vv
```

Also verified with a minimal multipart reproduction matching the issue report: after the fix, the request no longer raises `RequestNotRead` and instead reaches the expected `ConnectError`.

## Scope

This PR is limited to the Python SDK transport fix and its targeted tests.

## Motivation

`Cubelet` currently emits noisy TOML unknown-key warnings during startup when it reads the network plugin config through a partial bootstrap struct.

These warnings do not affect functionality, but they are misleading. They make the network plugin config appear invalid, even though the same full config is later accepted by the actual network plugin.

## Reproduction

Restart `cubelet` with the default config containing a full `[plugins."io.cubelet.internal.v1.network"]` section:

```bash
systemctl restart cube-sandbox-cubelet.service
journalctl -u cube-sandbox-cubelet.service -b -n 200 | grep 'Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin'
```

Example output:

```text
level=warning msg="Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin" error="strict mode: fields in the document are missing in the target struct" key=object_dir plugin=io.cubelet.internal.v1.network
level=warning msg="Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin" error="strict mode: fields in the document are missing in the target struct" key=redis_conf_path plugin=io.cubelet.internal.v1.network
level=warning msg="Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin" error="strict mode: fields in the document are missing in the target struct" key=report_stat_interval_in_sec plugin=io.cubelet.internal.v1.network
level=warning msg="Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin" error="strict mode: fields in the document are missing in the target struct" key=stream_block_time plugin=io.cubelet.internal.v1.network
level=warning msg="Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin" error="strict mode: fields in the document are missing in the target struct" key=stream_key plugin=io.cubelet.internal.v1.network
level=warning msg="Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin" error="strict mode: fields in the document are missing in the target struct" key=stream_name_prefix plugin=io.cubelet.internal.v1.network
level=warning msg="Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin" error="strict mode: fields in the document are missing in the target struct" key=tap_init_num plugin=io.cubelet.internal.v1.network
level=warning msg="Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin" error="strict mode: fields in the document are missing in the target struct" key=watch_stream plugin=io.cubelet.internal.v1.network
```

## Root Cause

The Cubelet startup path decodes the full `io.cubelet.internal.v1.network` plugin section into a partial bootstrap struct that only declares a subset of the plugin's TOML keys.

Because plugin config decoding runs in strict mode first, every valid key that is missing from the partial bootstrap struct is reported as an unknown-key warning before the decode falls back.

## What this PR changes

- reuses the existing full `network.Config` when reading the network plugin config for Cubelet bootstrap
- keeps the bootstrap behaviour unchanged
- stops valid network plugin config keys from being reported as misleading unknown-key warnings during Cubelet startup

## Testing

Added a targeted unit test to cover decoding a full `io.cubelet.internal.v1.network` plugin config section through the Cubelet bootstrap config loader.

The test verifies that valid network plugin config keys are accepted when loading the bootstrap config, instead of being treated as unknown keys due to partial struct decoding.

Targeted test:

```bash
go test -vet=off ./cmd/cubelet -run TestLoadNetworkPluginBootstrapConfigDecodesNetworkPluginSection
```

Also validated on a Linux node by replacing the cubelet binary and fully restarting the service:

```bash
systemctl restart cube-sandbox-cubelet.service
journalctl -u cube-sandbox-cubelet.service -b -n 200 | grep 'Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin'
```

After the restart, the grep command produced no matching startup warnings.

## Out of Scope

A similar warning can also be reproduced in some cubecli network-agent related commands, such as:

```bash
cubecli container taps | grep "Ignoring unknown key in TOML for plugin"
```

That path is intentionally left unchanged in this PR because it goes through a separate `cubecli` network-agent config loading path. Fixing it cleanly would require deciding whether `cubecli` should also reuse the network plugin's full `network.Config`, or whether the CLI should keep its own bootstrap/agent-specific config shape.

This PR is limited to the Cubelet startup path to avoid mixing that broader CLI config-sharing decision into this fix.

## Documentation

No documentation update is needed because this change only removes misleading warnings during config decoding. It does not change command behaviour, plugin config shape, APIs, or runtime semantics.

## perf: optimize TAP fd acquisition hot path

### Motivation

On the sandbox creation hot path, `GetTapFile` always executes the full `restoreTap` flow (including netlink `LinkByName` lookup, `LinkSetUp`/`SetMTU`, TC filter `AttachFilter`, and ARP entry write), even when the TAP device is already in the pool and fully configured. These redundant operations become a significant performance bottleneck in bulk creation scenarios.

### Changes

1. **Return ifindex to avoid redundant netlink lookup**  
   `GetTapFile` now also returns the tap's kernel ifindex, so callers (cubelet) can skip an independent `netlink LinkByName` query.

2. **Fast re-open fd for pooled taps**  
   For pooled taps that are fully configured but whose fd was closed while idle, take the fast path: only two syscalls (`open + TUNSETIFF`), skipping the entire `restoreTap` (netlink lookup, MTU set, TC filter attach, ARP entry write).

3. **Recovery path**  
   When the agent restarts with no in-memory state or the tap is held by an external process, fall back to the full `restoreTap` to ensure correctness.

4. **`indexFallback` helper**  
   Prefers the persisted ifindex; falls back to the live tap's index when unset.

5. **pprof debugging (disabled by default)**  
   New `--pprof-listen` flag to enable the pprof HTTP server for analyzing mutex/block contention.

6. **Concurrency test coverage**  
   Added `local_service_concurrency_test.go` covering `EnsureNetwork`/`ReleaseNetwork` correctness under parallel goroutines (with race detection).

### Benchmark Results

**Test environment:** Tencent Cloud BMI5 (Inspur SA5212M5) × dual Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8255C @ 2.50GHz (48 cores, 96 threads), 375Gi RAM, OpenCloudOS 9.4, kernel 6.6.119

| Metric         | Baseline (old) | This PR   | Improvement |
| -------------- | -------------- | --------- | ----------- |
| **Total P50**  | 106.1          | **92.0**  | **↓ 13%**   |
| **Net P50**    | 35.3           | **23.1**  | **↓ 35%**   |
| **Net P99**    | 86.6           | **51.2**  | **↓ 41%**   |
| **Throughput** | 194.8          | **209.8** | **↑ 8%**    |
| **CPU**        | 0.1%           | **0.2%**  | Negligible ✅ |

> Significant improvements across the board: P50 down 13%, Network P50 down 35%, Network P99 down 41%, throughput up 8%, with minimal CPU impact (0.2%).

### Changed Files

| File                                                            | Change                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `network-agent/internal/service/tap_fd_provider.go`             | GetTapFile now returns ifindex + fast/recovery path     |
| `network-agent/internal/service/netdevice.go`                   | Added openTapFdByName, indexFallback, extracted netlink hook vars |
| `network-agent/internal/service/local_service.go`               | Added TapIfIndex persistence, adapted to new GetTapFile signature |
| `network-agent/internal/service/tap_lifecycle.go`               | Adapted to interface change                             |
| `network-agent/cmd/network-agent/main.go`                       | Added pprof HTTP server                                 |
| `network-agent/internal/fdserver/server.go`                     | Adapted to interface change                             |
| `network-agent/internal/service/local_service_concurrency_test.go` | New concurrency test file                            |
| `network-agent/internal/service/local_service_test.go`          | Adapted to interface change                             |
| `network-agent/internal/service/tap_lifecycle_test.go`          | Adapted to interface change                             |
| `CubeNet/cubevs/map.go`                                         | Related adaptation                                      |
| `CubeNet/cubevs/netpolicy.go`                                   | Related adaptation                                      |
| `CubeNet/cubevs/tap.go`                                         | Related adaptation                                      |
| `Cubelet/network/plugin_tap.go`                                 | Adapted to new GetTapFile signature                     |
| `network-agent/go.mod`                                          | Dependency update                                       |

- [x] Unit tests pass
- [x] Concurrency tests (race detection) pass

body:
…GuestError

The native virtiofs server in `Fs::init_backend_fs_server` was building its `passthrough::Config` with the upstream-default `migration_on_error` of `Abort`. Under that policy, if any inode referenced by a snapshot fails to resolve at restore time (for example, because the host-side backing file was deleted between snapshot and restore), the entire live restore is torn down — even though every other inode is still healthy.

Switch the policy to `MigrationOnError::GuestError`. Per-inode failures now surface to the guest as ordinary FS errors (ENOENT / EIO) on the specific affected paths, while the VM as a whole, and the rest of the shared filesystem, continue to operate normally. This matches the production expectation that a single missing or partially-dirty file must not be allowed to kill an in-flight live migration of an otherwise healthy sandbox.

Add a sequential integration test that covers the
snapshot-then-delete-backing-file-then-restore scenario, locking in that the restore succeeds, the surviving files remain readable, the mount still accepts new operations, and only access to the deleted file surfaces an error to the guest.

A paused/frozen VM cannot serve its runtime (ttrpc) API, so the shim rejects the regular per-container delete with "sandbox not in normal state" and the sandbox can never be removed (error 130593/130506).

Route teardown of paused sandboxes through a binary force-delete that SIGKILLs the shim (reaping the in-process cube-hypervisor) and detaches it from the runtime manager, letting containerd's dead-shim cleanup reclaim the VM workdir and pause snapshot:

- Destroy: select the SkipRuntimeAPI path when the sandbox is paused and factor the force-delete into destroySandboxByBinary.
- CleanUp (GC reconcile / workflow compensation): mirror the same path so a paused sandbox is reclaimed instead of looping forever on "shim process still Exists".

Verified end-to-end (running -> pause -> delete): RetCode 200, shim and VMM reaped, VM workdir / pause snapshot / bundle all reclaimed, no error spam.

### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR refactors the CLS metric reporting loop in the `Cubelet` plugin by introducing a random jitter to the wait timer. 

#### The Problem (Cubelet Upgrade Scenario)
In cubelet deployment or rolling upgrade scenarios, thousands of Node/Cubelet instances are restarted concurrently.
Under the previous fixed-ticker implementation, all instances would wake up and report their first batch of CLS metrics at the exact same second. 
This causes severe traffic spikes (a "thundering herd") capable of overwhelming downstream metric collectors and API gateways.

### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes concurrent surge risks during large scale `Cubelet` upgrades.

body:
## Summary

Reduce peak disk usage from **~4.2X** image size down to **~1.2X** (72% reduction) during template image-to-ext4 builds.

## Changes

### Phase 1 (default on)

1. **Pipe-streamed export** — eliminate intermediate `rootfs.tar` file by connecting `docker export | tar -xf -` via Go pipe
2. **Early workDir cleanup** — remove work directory before ext4 creation instead of defer-to-end
3. **Precise ext4 sizing** — replace power-of-2 alignment with 256 MiB boundary, adding triple-overhead model (fixed + percentage + per-file)
4. **Direct-to-storeDir export** — skip relocate step on local filesystems, detect NFS/CIFS via statfs magic for fallback
5. **Disk-space pre-check** — fail-fast with configurable safety margin

### Phase 2 (opt-in, default off)

6. **Loop-mount streaming build** — `CUBEMASTER_LOOP_MOUNT_EXT4_ENABLED=true`, auto-detects CAP_SYS_ADMIN and /dev/loop-control

### Security hardening
- Reject `-` prefixed image references
- Add `--` separator to all docker/mount/umount/losetup invocations
- Mount with `nosuid,noexec,nodev,noatime` for loop devices
- `sync.Once` for idempotent umount and losetup detach

### Other improvements
- SHA256 computation uses 4 MiB buffer
- Cleanup failures logged at WARN level

## Verification

| Metric | Old (power-of-2) | New | Improvement |
|--------|-----------------|-----|-------------|
| Peak disk (5 GiB image) | ~20.8 GiB (4.2X) | ~3.9 GiB (~1.2X) | **↓ 72%** |
| ext4 size (rust:1.77) | ~4 GiB | 2.0 GiB | ↓ 50% |
| Actual disk usage | ~3.3 GiB | 1.4 GiB | ↓ 58% |

Tested with alpine (~8 MiB), mysql:8.0 (~786 MiB), golang:1.22 (~754 MiB), rust:1.77 (~1.32 GiB) on x86_64.

All existing unit tests pass.

## Motivation

On the nodemeta path, CubeMaster can keep a node healthy after `cubelet` stops reporting heartbeats because the last reported `Ready=True` fact is reused as the current health result.

This makes stale nodes look healthy in control-plane reads and can leave them eligible for scheduling decisions longer than expected.

## What this PR changes

- derive current node health from the last reported readiness fact plus heartbeat freshness
- make nodemeta reads return the current effective `healthy` result instead of a stale cached value
- make `healthy=false` explicit in API output
- expose `unhealthy_reason` for `HeartbeatExpired` and `ReportedNotReady`
- make `localcache` read paths refresh health from cached facts without mutating shared cached nodes
- apply the same health refresh logic to `GetNodesByIp`
- make prefilter skip stale metadata / metric nodes instead of only logging timeout

## Testing

```bash
go test -vet=off ./pkg/localcache ./pkg/nodemeta ./pkg/selector/prefilter
```

Manual validation:

- stale heartbeat is returned as `healthy=false`
- `unhealthy_reason` distinguishes `HeartbeatExpired` and `ReportedNotReady`
- `/internal/meta/nodes/{id}` and `/internal/node` reflect the same health semantics

## Documentation

No standalone documentation update is included in this PR. However, this change does affect the JSON shape of node responses: `healthy=false` is now emitted explicitly instead of being omitted.

## Related issue

Fixes #454

body:
When network-agent restarts, recover() can mistakenly treat a TAP that is still held by a running sandbox as abnormal or stale, removing its ifindex_to_mvmmeta BPF map entry. Egress traffic from the sandbox then hits a NULL lookup in the from_cube program and is silently dropped via TC_ACT_SHOT. This produced the observed behavior where stopping network-agent kept the network alive but restarting it broke it.

Root cause:
restoreTap() unconditionally tried to acquire the tap fd via TUNSETIFF even when IFF_LOWER_UP was set (i.e. sandbox already owned the fd). With IFF_ONE_QUEUE the kernel rejects the second open with EBUSY. The TAP was pushed into the abnormal pool and never entered the recovered set, so the second pass of recover() concluded the sandbox state was stale and called cubevsDelTAPDevice, wiping the BPF map entry and the persisted state.

Fix:
- restoreTap: skip getTapFd when tap.InUse is true (IFF_LOWER_UP set) and reuse the fd held by the existing owner. With this, restoreTap no longer fails with EBUSY for live sandboxes, the TAP joins the recovered set, and the stale-cleanup branch never fires.
- GetTapFile: if restoreTap intentionally returned without an fd, surface a clear error to the caller instead of handing back a nil *os.File.

body:
Add a small Python CLI (`examples/runner`) to discover, run, and assert the example scripts under `examples/`. Each example declares its setup, steps, and expected outcomes in a `cube-example.yaml` manifest; the runner executes them against a running CubeSandbox deployment and emits JSON + Markdown reports.

## Motivation

The `examples/` directory ships ~12 demos, but previously each had to be run by hand (`cd`, `pip install`, `python xxx.py`) with no automated pass/fail check. There was no easy way, on every release, to verify the shipped examples still execute and produce the expected output.

## What this adds

- `cube_examples.manifest` — parse/validate `cube-example.yaml`
- `cube_examples.runner` — execute setup + ordered steps, assert exit code / stdout substrings
- `cube_examples.report` — JSON (machine) + Markdown (release-notes) reports
- `cube_examples.cli` — `list` / `run` subcommands, tag & name filters, template alias mapping
- A `cube-example.yaml` for each current example. Examples needing external credentials/services (OpenAI agents, dev-sidecar) default to `skip`.

## Usage

```bash
cd examples/runner
pip install -r requirements.txt

# List examples
python -m cube_examples list --tags smoke

# Run smoke + sdk examples against a deployment
python -m cube_examples run \
  --api-url http://<node-ip>:3000 \
  --template code=<template-id> \
  --ssl-cert-file /root/.local/share/mkcert/rootCA.pem \
  --tags smoke sdk \
  --report-md report.md --report-json report.json
```

The runner injects the env vars the example scripts already read (`E2B_API_URL`/`CUBE_API_URL`, `E2B_API_KEY`, `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`). Examples that require a template alias not supplied on the command line are reported as `skipped` (not failed), so partial runs are safe.

## Release verification flow

```
build one-click bundle -> install on a clean node -> create a template
  -> python -m cube_examples run --tags smoke sdk --report-md release-report.md
  -> attach report to release notes
```

## Verified

Tested end-to-end against a fresh control-plane deployment:
- `code-sandbox-quickstart` and `host-mount` pass.
- The runner correctly surfaces real environment issues (missing SSL cert, image lacking `curl`, template mismatch) with actionable failure detail in the report.

Exit codes: `0` all passed (skips OK), `1` any failure/error, `2` bad args / no match.

body:
disableGRO() previously issued a single ETHTOOL_SGRO ioctl against cfg.EthName. For bond uplinks this only flips the feature flag on the bond netdev — GRO actually happens in the NAPI poll of the underlying slaves, so packets still get coalesced before reaching cubevs/tap and the original goal (preserve MTU-sized frames into the guest) is not met.

Resolve the configured interface, recursively walk into bond slaves and vlan parents, and call ethtool SGRO on every underlying netdev as well as the device itself (to keep the upper-layer feature flag consistent). For anything else (physical NIC, virtio-net, etc.) we fall through the default branch and just operate on the device itself, matching the previous behavior.

A per-slave failure is logged at Warn and the first error is returned, mirroring the existing Warn-only handling at the call site so a single bad NIC does not block service startup.

body:
### Summary

The shim daemon could finish its parent-side `start` handshake **before**
its ttrpc server had bound and started listening on the control socket.
When that happened, the caller dialed a socket that did not exist yet and
the container failed to start:

```
failed to start shim: start failed: failed to create TTRPC connection:
dial unix /run/containerd/s/<id>: connect: no such file or directory
```

This was intermittent and more likely under load or on slower hosts, and a
failed start could leave an **orphaned shim process** still holding the
listening socket and host resources.

### Root cause

`Log::new()` runs very early during shim-daemon startup and redirected
**both** stdout (fd 1) and stderr (fd 2) onto an internal `UnixDatagram`
via `dup2`:

```rust
dup2(writer.as_raw_fd(), std::io::stdout().as_raw_fd()).expect("dup stdout failed");
dup2(writer.as_raw_fd(), std::io::stderr().as_raw_fd()).expect("dup stdout failed");
```

In the `containerd-shim` bootstrap protocol, **fd 1 of the daemon is the
readiness pipe**. The parent `start` process copies the daemon's stdout to
its own stdout until EOF; reaching EOF is what tells the parent the daemon
is ready, after which the parent prints the bound socket address back to
the caller.

By `dup2`-ing over fd 1 before the ttrpc server was listening, `Log::new()`
closed the original pipe write-end early. The parent then observed EOF
prematurely and reported the socket as ready while the server had not yet
called `bind()/listen()`. The caller dialed a non-existent socket → the
`ENOENT` ("no such file or directory") TTRPC failure above.

### Fix

Take over **only stderr (fd 2)** in `Log::new()`. The `containerd-shim`
crate already calls `signal_server_started()` after `server.start()`,
which performs `dup2(STDERR -> STDOUT)` **once the ttrpc server is
listening**. That:

- redirects stdout onto our logging datagram (logging still captured), and
- closes the readiness pipe at the correct moment, so the parent reports
  readiness only after the socket is actually bound.

The fix contains no retries, sleeps, or polling — it removes the premature
fd-1 redirect and lets the crate's intended handshake run, eliminating the
race at its source.

### Verification

Ran a create/delete stress loop against the built shim:

| Round | Config | Success | TTRPC failures | Leaked shims | Orphaned sockets |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20 concurrent × 200 create+delete | 100% | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 50 concurrent × 500 create+delete | 75.8% | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Across 700 create cycles (including a 50-way concurrent burst) there were
**zero** `failed to create TTRPC connection` errors, **zero** leaked shim
processes, and **zero** new orphaned sockets.

The failures in round 2 were all backpressure from the control plane
(`no more resource`) when too many microVMs were requested concurrently on
one host — expected over-subscription behavior, unrelated to the shim
startup path.

### Risk / compatibility

- Logging behavior is preserved: stdout is still routed to the logging
  datagram, just at the correct point (after `server.start()`).
- No public API or config change.
- Restores the upstream `containerd-shim` readiness contract rather than
  working around it, so the change is conservative and low-risk.

body:
## Summary

- Route Python SDK `commands.run()` through envd `process.Process/Start` instead of wrapping `subprocess.run()` with `run_code()`.
- Preserve stdout/stderr/exit code boundaries by parsing envd Connect stream events directly.
- Move Python filesystem read/write helpers to envd `/files` APIs.
- Add unit coverage for Connect envelope parsing, command execution, timeouts, and filesystem read/write behavior.

## Motivation

The previous Python SDK command runner serialized command stdout and the exit code over the same stdout stream. When command stdout did not end with a newline, the exit code could be appended to the stdout tail, corrupting user output silently.

Using envd's process API aligns the Python SDK with the Go SDK implementation and avoids guessing the exit code from stdout contents.

## Tests

- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_sandbox.py -q`
  - Passed on `cubesandbox002` under `/data/cubesandbox/code/max_test/CubeSandbox/sdk/python`
